replacements.reason: Close the host-only anonymous PowerPC-layout fighter flag aggregate before character-specific runtime variables.
Match the retained damage-fall sound-array pointer assigned from FtSFX and dereferenced after the fall transition.
Decode the opcode and value from the original big-endian PowerPC action-command bytes before native dispatch.

Map the MotionState packed u32 initializer onto the original PowerPC byte fields on little-endian i686: move_id is the high byte, x9 keeps MSB-first named bits, and xA/xB retain their source byte positions.

Map every PowerPC animation-flag accessor onto the same numeric bits of the endian-normalized i686 u32. Fighter_ChangeMotionState at GALE01 0x80069C48 loads the big-endian halfword at fp+596 and 0x80069C50 extracts its bits 6 through 8; after u32 normalization those are raw bits 6 through 8, immediately above the six-bit FighterKind field.
Map the action animation flag accessor onto the normalized host-order u32 so partial-animation reloads retain the GALE01 loop bit instead of interpreting the low host byte as an i686 u8 bitfield.
Limit reverse scalar storage order to the packed asset command overlay and retain host layout for all following runtime structures.

Normalize all four byte lanes of the shared fighter/item motion word while preserving PowerPC MSB-first bits within each byte. Numeric values, move IDs, category flags and signed high-byte access must describe the same word on i686; both runtime-created temporary words and stored fighter/item words use this type.

Map all fighter attack-history flag accessors onto the numeric high 16 bits of x2084. Items copy this complete word through xDA4_word and share Struct2074 consumers; preserve the low 16 bits instead of shifting flags into them on little-endian hosts.
